data.title: ZTEST Electronics Inc. Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results With 34.9% Revenue Growth and 39.2% Increase in Net Income
data.description:
NORTH YORK, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / ZTEST Electronics Inc. ( ZTSTF ) ("ZTEST" or the "Company") (CSE:ZTE)(OTCID:ZTSTF) is pleased to announce its unaudited financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the three months ended September 30, 2026, with revenues of $2,459,431, an increase of 34.9% over the first quarter of fiscal 2026, and net income increasing 39.2% to $329,879 ($0.009 per share).

Gross margin for the quarter rose 34.9% to $1,049,233 from $777,694 in Q1 2026, with the gross margin percentage maintained at 42.7%. EBITDA for the quarter increased 40.5% to $567,593, and operating cash flow, before changes in non-cash working capital, increased 56.1% to $503,898 from $322,798 in Q1 2026.

The first quarter marked the fourth consecutive quarter of year over year revenue growth. Turnkey revenues increased by more than 36% and non-turnkey revenues by almost 12%, and revenues for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2026 reached $9,835,807, an increase of 21.1% over the comparable period one year earlier.

Net income as a percentage of revenue improved to 13.4% from 13.0% in Q1 2026. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by only 4.4% to $499,995 despite the 34.9% increase in revenues.

The Company ended the quarter with cash and cash equivalents of $5,844,750, an increase of $380,045 (7.0%) since June 30, 2026, and during the quarter added $505,362 (7.8%) to working capital and $476,678 (6.6%) to shareholders' equity. The Company has no long-term debt, and its $1,000,000 bank operating line remained undrawn.

The Company also continued its normal course issuer bid, repurchasing and cancelling 99,000 common shares during the quarter and a further 158,500 common shares after quarter end.

Dave Barnett, CEO, commented, "We are pleased that fiscal 2027 has started by building on the momentum established last year. First quarter revenues grew by almost 35%, and that growth carried through to the bottom line, with gross margin percentage holding steady at 42.7% and net income rising more than 39%. These results were achieved in a marketplace that continues to be disrupted by tariffs and supply chain pressures, and they reflect the value our customers place on Permatech's quality, flexibility and service.

With more than $5.8 million in cash, no debt and growing working capital, ZTEST is well positioned to build on this momentum, both by supporting continued organic growth at Permatech and by evaluating strategic growth opportunities, while maintaining our commitment to enhancing shareholder value."

ZTEST Electronics Inc. ( ZTSTF ), through its wholly owned subsidiary Permatech Electronics Corporation ("Permatech"), offers Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) to a wide range of customers. Permatech's offering includes Printed Circuit Board (PCB) Assembly, Materials Management and Testing services. Permatech operates from an ISO 9001:2015 certified facility in North York, Ontario, Canada. Permatech is a contract assembler of complex circuit boards, serving customers in the Medical, Power, Computer, Telecommunications, Wireless, Industrial, Trucking, Wearables and Consumer Electronics markets. It specializes in servicing customers who are looking for high yield and require high quality and rapid-turnaround to produce high complexity products.

data.title: INTURAI RELEASES NEW CAPABILITY TO SUPPORT CUSTOMER DEPLOYMENTS AND COMMERCIAL ROLLOUT
data.description:
(CSE: URAI / OTC: URAIF / FSE: 3QG0) 
investor@inturai.com

Highlights

  • Inturai's ( URAIF ) sensors can now tell which floor of a building a person or device is on. The innovative, proprietary capability is available now, extending the Company's spatial intelligence platform to multi-floor buildings.
  • In the Company's testing in multi-floor buildings, the capability accurately detected the correct floor. It is switched on remotely on sensors already installed, with no site survey and no new equipment.
  • The release supports the Company's live commercial and pilot deployments and unlocks parts of its growing pipeline, with new early-stage leads building among household name retailers and aged care providers since the first-outlet go-live with a Southeast Asian Pizza Hut operator.

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Inturai Ventures Corp. ( URAIF ) (the "Company") (CSE: URAI) (OTC: URAIF) (FSE: 3QG0) is pleased to announce that its spatial intelligence platform now works floor by floor in multi-level buildings. The Company's sensors can tell which floor of a building a person or device is on, and report only what is happening on that floor. The new capability, Precision Floor-Level Wireless Intelligence, is available now and is designed for customers operating sites on more than one level.

The release follows the Company's go-live at the first outlet of a Southeast Asian Pizza Hut operator, announced on November 17, 2026. Live commercial and pilot deployments are now running. Since that announcement, the Company has been building new leads with household name retailers and aged care providers. These discussions are at an early stage, and there is no assurance they will lead to agreements. Floor-level sensing supports those deployments and unlocks parts of the pipeline where sites run across more than one floor. It can be applied beyond retail and aged care, and the Company expects it to support commercialisation in the other markets it serves.

Wireless signals pass through floors and ceilings, so a sensor on one floor can pick up a phone on the floor above and treat it as if it were on the same level. In a multi-storey store, care facility or office, that puts visitor counts, alerts and equipment locations on the wrong floor. The Company's sensors now learn each building on their own and ignore anything from the floors above and below. The capability is switched on remotely on sensors already installed, with no site survey and no new equipment.

The capability was developed in-house and builds on the Company's proprietary sensing methods and the intellectual property framework it announced in February 2026. Conventional approaches to floor-level accuracy rely on manual site surveys or specialised hardware, and the Company's innovative approach needs neither. The Company is considering patent protection for the capability, and there is no assurance that a patent will be filed or granted.

Retailers get visitor numbers they can rely on for each level of a store. Aged care providers know which floor an alert has come from, so carers go to the right place first. Businesses tracking tagged equipment can see which floor each item is on. It can also reduce cost for customers who would otherwise need a separate system for each floor.

In the Company's testing in multi-floor buildings, the capability accurately detected the correct floor. Performance varies with building type, conditions and device type. Organisations can contact Inturai ( URAIF ) to switch on floor-level sensing at their existing sites, and further updates will be provided as material developments occur.

data.title: Canada's Job Vacancies Rise, BMO Says
data.description:
06:54 AM EST, 11/27/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Canada's job vacancy rate increased to 2.9% in September, marking its first rise after more than four years of almost uninterrupted decline, according to BMO Capital Markets in a note after Thursday's SEPH payrolls data.

Despite remaining well below its late-2021/early-2022 peak, the rise indicates a modest improvement in labor demand, even as the Labour Force Survey recorded employment declines for a third consecutive month, wrote BMO in a Thursday note.

The rise has been concentrated in some less expected sectors, with professional and technical services, retail trade and manufacturing posting some of the largest annual increases in vacancy rates, said the bank.

In contrast, vacancies have declined in healthcare and construction, although both sectors continue to record above-average rates. Accommodation and food services saw the sharpest increase, up 0.6 percentage point yearly to 4.7%, also the highest vacancy rate among all sectors.

Education was unchanged at 1.1%, remaining the lowest.

The vote took place at the Scheme Meeting held on November 27, 2026.

The resolution to approve the Scheme was passed by 99.40% of the votes cast by Ausgold ( AUSGF ) shareholders. Subject to Court approval, the Transaction is expected to become effective on December 2, 2026, and close on December 11, 2026.

Under the Scheme, Ausgold ( AUSGF ) shareholders will receive 0.03365 common shares of OceanaGold ( OGC ) for each share of Ausgold ( AUSGF ) held (the "Scheme Consideration"). Ausgold ( AUSGF ) shareholders had the opportunity to elect to receive the Scheme Consideration value in cash at A$1.36 per Ausgold ( AUSGF ) share, subject to scale-back based on a maximum available cash pool for the Transaction of A$194 million (US$129 million)1. Upon completion of the Transaction, it is expected that Ausgold ( AUSGF ) shareholders will own around 6% to 8% of OceanaGold ( OGC ).

06:28 AM EST, 11/27/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Treasuries were lower in early Friday trading, while US equity futures continued to recover after the Thanksgiving break and oil prices edged higher, Commerzbank Research said in a note.

President Donald Trump dismissed the pre-midterm election gross domestic product figures as "fake" and called for an investigation, wrote Commerzbank in the note.

The US government remained $511 billion below the debt ceiling as of Tuesday, said the bank.

President Trump said he had urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression ... throughout Europe." Meanwhile, the United States is postponing plans to restructure its military presence in Europe, according to Politico.

The US dollar strengthened, added Commerzbank.

European Union leaders agreed to recommend Pablo Hernandez de Cos for the European Central Bank presidency.

The EU plans to introduce new loans and grants from the second half of 2027 to bolster defense capabilities and reduce reliance on the US, with the size of the package yet to be determined, according to Bloomberg.

EU budget talks collapsed after French President Emmanuel Macron said he wouldn't approve an unbalanced deal, said the bank. France and Germany are pushing for an agreement by year-end to safeguard the next EU budget and Ukraine funding against a potential far-right Marine Le Pen victory in the French presidential election next year, according to Reuters.

China's State Council reiterated its commitment to supporting capital markets in a midday statement, added Commerzbank.

data.description:
06:21 AM EST, 11/26/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Treasury futures remained under pressure in early Thursday trading, while US equity futures moved higher and oil extended its rally, with Brent topping $95 a barrel, according to Commerzbank Research in a note.

The Federal Reserve's Beige Book reported moderate economic growth and modest wage increases, partly reflecting cost-of-living adjustments and rising benefit costs, wrote Commerzbank in the note.

data.title: AgentLocker Study: 4,746 AI Tools Now Compete for $3 Trillion in Annual US Payroll
data.description:
Image: AgentLocker Study 4,746 AI Tools Now Compete for $3 Trillion in Annual US Payroll

Live analysis mapping thousands of AI products against US Bureau of Labor Statistics data shows 62% of the AI software market is chasing just three job functions.

MANCHESTER, United Kingdom, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AgentLocker, an AI agents and tools directory and community platform, today published the AgentLocker AI Jobs Automation Index, a live data report mapping 4,746 tracked AI tools against US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) employment, salary, and 2024–2034 job outlook figures.

The analysis reveals that AI software products now target 16 major job functions representing an estimated $3.0 trillion in annual US payroll—making cognitive work the largest software market in history.

While public debate often frames artificial intelligence as an even threat across the entire workforce, the index exposes a heavily concentrated gold rush. Nearly two-thirds of all tracked AI products compete for the same narrow slice of white-collar tasks, leaving massive sectors of the US economy largely untouched by AI software competition.

Key Findings from the Index

  • Business Operations leads all sectors: 1,393 AI tools—29.4% of every product tracked in the AgentLocker directory—are built to automate or assist with Business Operations.
  • A remarkably narrow gold rush: 62.0% of all AI tools target just three job functions: Business Operations, Content & Writing, and Marketing.
  • Writers face the highest tool-to-worker ratio: Content & Writing workers are the most outnumbered, with 532.8 AI tools for every 100,000 US workers in the field.
  • Massive competition in customer support: America's 2,814,000 customer service workers (median salary $46,590) now face 893 dedicated AI products built to handle their core workflows.
  • Healthcare remains the least-targeted sector: Healthcare sees just 1.8 AI tools per 100,000 US workers—296 times fewer than Content & Writing.

Image: AgentLocker Study 4,746 AI Tools Now Compete for $3 Trillion in Annual US Payroll

"Everyone talks about AI disrupting the labor market in abstract terms, so we wanted to put hard numbers behind where AI builders are actually aiming," said Oliver Dale, CEO at AgentLocker. "Seeing 4,746 tools chase $3 trillion in annual US payroll shows just how massive this software shift is—but the data also proves that AI exposure is not evenly distributed, and exposure alone doesn't automatically equal job loss."

Exposure vs. Job Loss

The index pairs tool counts with an editorial 0–100 AI exposure score across 25 specific occupations, estimating how much of each role's core O*NET tasks current AI products can perform. AgentLocker emphasizes that the $3.0 trillion figure represents the total estimated payroll associated with AI-targeted job functions rather than predicted job losses or wages expected to disappear. By plotting AI exposure directly against BLS 2024–2034 employment projections, the report distinguishes between high-exposure roles projected to shrink and high-exposure roles still projected to grow.

Methodology and Availability

All 4,746 AgentLocker directory listings were categorized and mapped to 16 broad job functions, with tools counted across multiple functions where their capabilities span several types of work. Employment and wage figures are derived from public US Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) data matched to representative occupation groups.

The full interactive report, rankings, and methodology are publicly available at: https://agentlocker.ai/stats/jobs-ai-could-replace

data.title: Faex Health CEO Landon Nattrass to Address the Future of AI-Enabled Preventive Healthcare at HITLAB Fall Innovators Summit
data.description:
Faex Health is leveraging artificial intelligence and smartphone technology to democratize access to digestive health insights and advance preventive healthcare

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Faex Health Co-Founder and CEO Landon Nattrass will showcase how artificial intelligence, computer vision, and smartphone technology can turn everyday biological and behavioral data into meaningful digestive health insights at the HITLAB Fall 2026 Innovators Summit on Thursday, Dec. 3, at the Microsoft Technology Center in Times Square, New York City.

Faex Health, a digital health company pioneering AI-enabled digestive health monitoring, has developed a comprehensive technology platform that analyzes smartphone images of stool alongside information about an individual's nutrition, hydration, sleep, mood, stress, physical activity, medications, medical history, and other factors that can influence digestive health. The platform enables individuals to better understand their digestive wellness, identify patterns over time, and develop a more comprehensive picture of their overall health.

Addressing an audience of healthcare executives, researchers, investors, and technology innovators, Nattrass will explore how accessible, longitudinal digestive health monitoring could increase patient engagement, inform preventive care strategies, and create new opportunities for health systems, employers, payers, and government healthcare programs to engage the populations they serve.

"Technology has fundamentally changed how we engage with our health, from tracking our sleep and physical activity to monitoring our heart rate, yet we routinely flush one of the most valuable sources of information about our well-being," Nattrass said. "By leveraging a device that billions of people already carry, we have an opportunity to democratize access to digestive health information, empower individuals to take a more proactive role in their health, and help healthcare organizations engage patients beyond the traditional clinical setting."

Connecting Digestive Health to Whole-Person Wellness

A growing body of scientific research is examining the relationship between the gut microbiome and numerous aspects of physical and mental health, underscoring the importance of understanding digestive health within the broader context of an individual's well-being.

"Gut health extends far beyond digestion. Research is increasingly revealing connections between the gut microbiome and everything from depression and headaches to sleep quality, stress response, and immune function," said Ryan Ninness, co-founder and chief technology officer of Faex Health. "The relationship is bidirectional. Our daily behaviors can influence our digestive health, and our digestive health may influence how we feel and function. By bringing these data points together, we can help individuals better understand patterns and relationships that might otherwise go unnoticed."

Taking place Dec. 1–3, the HITLAB Fall Innovators Summit brings together leaders from across the healthcare ecosystem, including health systems, payers, life sciences companies, academic institutions and emerging technology companies, to examine the opportunities and challenges associated with bringing digital health innovations into clinical and commercial practice.

Central to the Faex Health platform is Felix, an AI-powered digestive health assistant that draws on curated scientific research and individual user information to provide personalized educational insights. By contextualizing stool image analysis with health history, symptoms, and lifestyle information, Felix helps users better understand their digestive wellness and prepare for more informed conversations with healthcare professionals.

Faex Health's technology ecosystem also includes a clinician-facing platform, research and analytics capabilities, and white-label integration opportunities designed to support adoption by healthcare organizations and integration into existing digital health platforms.

Advancing a More Proactive Approach to Digestive Health

Colorectal cancer is now the leading cause of cancer-related death among Americans under the age of 50, according to research from the American Cancer Society published in JAMA in January 2026. As the incidence of colorectal cancer among younger adults continues to raise concerns, there is a growing need to increase digestive health awareness and encourage engagement with healthcare providers before individuals reach the recommended age of 45 for routine colorectal cancer screening.

While conventional screening methods provide essential clinical information at specific points in time, Faex Health's technology enables individuals to build a longitudinal record of their digestive health, documenting changes and patterns that might otherwise go unrecorded.

The company is exploring how this approach could complement established care pathways, encourage timely conversations with healthcare professionals, and inform the development of future prescreening applications.

Building the Evidence Through Research and Strategic Collaboration

Faex Health's participation in the Summit underscores its commitment to advancing clinical research and evidence-based innovation, building on its strategic partnership with HITLAB to support clinical evidence development, regulatory preparation and U.S. commercialization. The company's broader research initiatives include FECAL-AI, an ongoing prospective clinical study at Hospital Dr. Sótero del Río in Santiago, Chile, evaluating the potential application of its AI-powered stool image analysis technology for colorectal neoplasia and colorectal cancer prescreening.

"The opportunity for AI in healthcare extends well beyond developing innovative technology. It is about making that technology accessible, establishing its clinical relevance, and demonstrating its value to the organizations responsible for delivering and financing healthcare," Nattrass continued. "Together with HITLAB and our clinical research partners, Faex Health is building the scientific foundation to advance that vision and expand access to AI-enabled digestive health technology worldwide."

Alongside its research initiatives, Faex Health continues to advance its commercialization strategy, with four signed agreements representing approximately 150,000 covered lives, including 50,000 active covered lives as of November 2026.

Faex Health's currently available consumer platform is designed to provide educational information and support digestive wellness monitoring. Its potential disease prescreening applications remain investigational. The technology is not intended to diagnose disease or replace established screening methods, medical advice, or care from a qualified healthcare professional.

Nattrass and Ninness will attend the HITLAB Fall Innovators Summit in person and are available for media interviews to discuss the evolving role of artificial intelligence in preventive healthcare, the relationship between digestive health and overall wellness, clinical evidence development and the potential for accessible digital health technologies to support healthcare delivery on a global scale.

For more information or to schedule an interview, contact Shawna Seldon at shawna@themaverickpr.com or +1 917-971-7852.

About Faex Health
Faex Health is a health technology company that has developed AI-powered solutions for preventive gastrointestinal health monitoring. Using computer vision, machine learning, and smartphone-based image analysis, the Faex platform helps users capture digestive health information, monitor patterns over time, and access personalized educational wellness insights. The company has developed solutions designed to support individuals, healthcare providers, health plans, employers, and population health organizations. Faex Health's investigational clinical applications are intended to complement established medical screening and diagnostic pathways, not replace them. For more information, visit FaexHealth.com. Download the Faex Health app on Apple Store for iOS and Google Play for Android. Continue the conversation on LinkedIn, Facebook, TikTok, X, Reddit, and Instagram.

Regulatory and Clinical Research Disclosure: Faex Health is investigational and has not received FDA clearance or approval. Its outputs are preliminary pre-screening indicators intended for health awareness and professional review, not medical diagnoses. All 18 indications have undergone internal validation, but these findings have not been independently replicated or peer reviewed as a complete panel. Clinical trials have not begun for the Ebola or H. pylori indications. The platform is not a substitute for laboratory testing, established screening protocols or professional medical evaluation.

Southeast Asia has attracted substantial data center investment from international operators, supported by the availability of land and power at competitive cost. The Company believes that this market offers long-term growth opportunities.

To develop that opportunity, the Board appointed Mr. Li Qiang as Chairman on December 11, 2025. Mr. Li has more than 20 years of experience in the data center and technology infrastructure industry, and he oversees the development of the Company's data center business.

data.title: Small Caps and Blue Chips Outpace Broader Market Through Midweek Session
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stock Preachers News Commentary - Stocks were mixed in afternoon trading Wednesday as the Russell 2000 and Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed to gains while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite slipped on the day. The small-cap and blue-chip benchmarks remain the strongest performers for the week, with volatility easing sharply from last Friday even as it ticked higher on the day. Treasury yields fell and gold firmed modestly as traders weighed a batch of new corporate headlines. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Deere & Company ( DE ) , Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) , Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. ( ANCTF ) , Amgen ( AMGN ) , and PayPal Holdings, Inc. ( PYPL ) .

The Dow Jones Industrial Average traded at 50,318.97 as of 2:54 p.m. ET Wednesday, up 300.27 points (0.60%) on the day and up 2,171.64 points (4.51%) on the week. The Russell 2000 stood at 2,707.27, up 22.33 points (0.83%) on the day and up 125.48 points (4.86%) on the week, its strongest weekly gain among the major benchmarks. The S&P 500 was little changed, down 9.70 points (0.13%) on the day at 7,191.39, though it remains up 281.00 points (4.07%) on the week. The Nasdaq Composite fell 124.20 points (0.52%) to 23,609.34 on the day while holding a 991.61 point (4.38%) weekly advance.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 1.45 points (5.50%) on the day to 27.81 but remains down 8.08 points (22.51%) on the week. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 96.39 points (1.09%) on the day to 8,736.11, still up 327.52 points (3.90%) on the week. The US 10-year Treasury yield slipped 6 basis points on the day and 7 basis points on the week to 4.84%.

Gold rose 0.10% on the day to $3,565.50 per ounce, up 1.43% on the week. WTI crude oil rose 1.68% on the day to $83.43 per barrel but remains down 0.65% on the week. Natural gas jumped 10.05% on the day to $3.657 per MMBtu, up 7.21% on the week. The US Dollar Index slipped 0.17% on the day and on the week to 103.63.

The full report includes the complete key levels ladder for each index, additional commodity and currency moves, and a look at sentiment heading into the final sessions of the week.

CONTINUED... Read this and more news for Deere & Company ( DE ) , Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) , Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. ( ANCTF ) , Amgen ( AMGN ) , and PayPal Holdings, Inc. ( PYPL ) at: https://stockpreachers.com/articles/small-caps-and-blue-chips-lead-at-the-midweek-turn/

In other industry developments and happenings in the market this week include:

Deere & Company ( DE ) Deere & Company ( DE ) reported net income of $1.051 billion, or $3.89 per share, for the fourth quarter ended November 1, 2026, compared with $1.065 billion, or $3.93 per share, a year earlier. For fiscal year 2026, net income attributable to Deere was $4.860 billion, or $17.95 per share, versus $5.027 billion, or $18.50 per share, in fiscal 2025. Worldwide net sales and revenues decreased 2% to $12.115 billion for the quarter and increased 4% to $47.704 billion for the full year.

Net income attributable to Deere for fiscal 2027 is forecasted to be in a range of $4.50 to $5.25 billion, which includes an estimated one-time, non-cash pension settlement charge of $0.25 to $0.40 billion. Read the release.

Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) reported fiscal first quarter 2027 total revenue of $3.44 billion, up 39% year over year. Next-Generation Security ARR grew 66% year over year to $9.73 billion, and remaining performance obligations grew 35% year over year to $21.0 billion. GAAP net income was $482 million, or $0.57 per diluted share, compared with $334 million, or $0.47 per diluted share, a year earlier.

The company also announced its intent to acquire Applied Compute, which it said will allow it to deliver secure open weight models to customers.

For fiscal 2027, the company expects total revenue in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. Read the release.

Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. ( ANCTF ) Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. ( ANCTF ) reported net earnings attributable to shareholders of $691.3 million for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, compared with $740.6 million a year earlier, or $0.75 per diluted share versus $0.79. Adjusted diluted net earnings per share were $0.84, an increase of 7.7% from $0.78 in the corresponding quarter last year. Total merchandise and service revenues were $4.8 billion, an increase of 1.7%.

He added that the company's voluntary tender offer for Zabka Group is now unconditional following receipt of all regulatory approvals, with the acceptance period ending December 2, 2026 and the offer expected to close on December 7, 2026. Read the release.

Amgen ( AMGN ) Amgen ( AMGN ) announced it has reached a settlement agreement with Bristol-Myers Squibb Company, E. R. Squibb & Sons, L.L.C., and Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. to resolve U.S. patent litigation related to ABP 206, Amgen's ( AMGN ) investigational biosimilar to OPDIVO. The company will launch ABP 206 in the U.S. on October 1, 2028, subject to FDA approval. The Biologics License Application has been submitted to and accepted for review by the FDA, which is expected to take action on the application by the end of 2026. Read the release.

PayPal Holdings, Inc. ( PYPL ) PayPal Holdings, Inc. ( PYPL ) announced several executive leadership appointments, including Claire Bramley as EVP and Chief Financial Officer, succeeding Jamie Miller, Chief Financial and Operating Officer. Kartik Mani will join as President and Head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo, Suzan Kereere will become President and Head of Payment Services & Crypto, and Juan Rio will join as EVP of AI Business Transformation & Operations on November 30, 2026.

The company also announced the appointment of Brian J. Lee to its Board of Directors, and said Aaron Webster, Chief Risk Officer, will depart the company, with Ratinder Bedi, SVP of Credit and Fraud Risk, serving as interim head of the Risk organization. Read the release.

data.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran businessÂ
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027. 

Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.

"After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week.

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture." 

"We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters. 

A spokesperson for the Brooklyn US Attorney's office, which brought the case, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither the White House nor China's embassy in Washington immediately responded to requests for comment on the verdict. 

Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference.

Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence.

FOUNDER'S DAUGHTER WAS DETAINED

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC ( HSBC ), Standard Chartered ( SCBFF ) and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

THE PROSECUTION CASE

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu ( FJTSF ) booth at a trade show to photograph a device. 

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. 

The defense argued that HSBC ( HSBC ) and the other banks knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for Huawei's business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development." 

The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries. 

(Additional reporting by Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Noeleen Walder and Will Dunham)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: 27 Years of Mobile Expertise: TCL P80 Ultra Named a CES Innovation Awards 2027 Honoree
data.description:
LAS VEGAS, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCL Mobile, a professional smartphone brand with 27 years of mobile engineering heritage, announced that the TCL P80 Ultra has been named a CES Innovation Awards® 2027 Honoree for Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps. The program received a record number of submissions, with nearly 4,000 entries reviewed by an elite panel of industry experts. The recognition was announced ahead of CES 2027, taking place Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The TCL P80 Ultra is the world's first smartphone to integrate TCL's NXTPAPER eye-comfort technology with an AMOLED display, addressing one of the industry's longstanding challenges: delivering advanced eye comfort without compromising flagship-level visual quality. Alongside the TCL P80 Pro, the TCL P80 Ultra is the only smartphone to hold SGS Low Glare Certification. It also carries TÜV Rheinland certification.

The achievement reflects decades of technology investment and industry participation that define TCL as a professional smartphone brand. TCL entered the mobile industry in 1999, making it one of China's earliest mobile brands. It acquired Alcatel's global handset business in 2004 and Palm in 2015. Today, TCL holds nearly 8,000 patents, including more than 2,000 in communication protocols, and works with ITU and 3GPP on 6G standardization, making it one of the few smartphone brands with expertise spanning 2G to 5G.

TCL's innovation is supported by a globally integrated research, manufacturing and sales model. The company operates China's largest single-site smartphone manufacturing facility in Huizhou, with an annual capacity of about 120 million units, alongside six dedicated overseas plants, giving it the most extensive global manufacturing footprint of any Chinese smartphone brand. TCL applies a 4-sigma quality process, compared with the 3-sigma standard typically associated with third-party assemblers.

A key differentiator is TCL CSOT, a top-three global supplier of smartphone panels. This gives TCL a rare advantage among Chinese smartphone brands with full in-house display manufacturing: display architecture, system-level tuning, and mass production are co-engineered from the start, accelerating innovations like NXTPAPER technology and enabling deeper hardware-software integration.

In mobile imaging, TCL has filed 30 international patents covering In-Sensor Zoom, Live Photo, and cross-device data transfer. Working with ArcSoft, TCL developed Quad Bayer Coding (QBC) with 10% higher zoom resolving power and Night TurboRAW with 8% higher low-light SNR. Its capabilities are further backed by end-to-end AI composition research with the University of Nottingham at CVPR 2025, a first-place win in the ECCV Mobile AI Challenge.

TCL has also established a strong AI foundation through collaborations across the global technology ecosystem. TCL was among the first Chinese smartphone brands to deploy Gemini and Circle to Search across its smartphone portfolio, and has also integrated Microsoft Azure AI capabilities, including Azure OpenAI models and Azure Speech Services, into its smartphone lineup. Co-developed with MediaTek and EAGLE LAB, this three-layer optimization spans NPU scheduling, imaging AI, display eye-comfort AI, multilingual voice, and on-device model adaptation.

The company's professional credentials extend beyond technology innovation. TCL works to TL 9000 telecom-grade quality standard, serves as a trusted quality partner to 54 major carriers worldwide and holds consecutive EcoVadis Gold Medals. It sells in more than 160 countries and regions and ranks among the top five smartphone shippers in North America.

"Awards make visible what usually stays inside the factory," said Vito Wang, General Manager of the TCL Mobile Terminal BU. "This one reflects a simple fact: We develop the technology, help shape the standards, make the displays and build the phones ourselves. That is what a professional smartphone brand means, not just one product, but 27 years of solving hard problems end to end."

That journey continues at CES 2027 in Las Vegas, with TCL bringing its latest mobile innovations to TCL's booth (#25008), where attendees can experience the TCL P80 Ultra alongside TCL's broader lineup, and also see the honoree showcase at the CES Innovation Awards Showcase in Venetian Expo, Hall A, Booth #50243.

TCL Mobile specializes in the research, development, and manufacturing of smartphones, tablets and connected devices. On a mission to deliver 5G for all, TCL Mobile helps its customers 'Inspire Greatness' in their lives through industry-leading technology and solutions. 

For more information, please visit: https://www.tcl.com/global/en/mobile

data.title: Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say
data.description:
BOSTON/NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday.

The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment, these people said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said on Monday that after talks with senior US officials, its board "is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

The abrupt U-turn, just days after the board vowed to look elsewhere for a successor, has also drawn US President Donald Trump and his administration into Nvidia's ( NVDA ) corporate governance. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares closed 31.5% higher on Monday even as it was becoming clear that the chipmaker's board acted under pressure from Trump and others, and the president took credit for the change.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces investigations, including by the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Justice Department, over issues ranging from its accounting to alleged chip smuggling. Nvidia ( NVDA ) press representatives did not immediately respond to questions for this story.

The situation undercuts the board's standing, said New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who helps manage retirement funds that hold some 5 million Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"They told us flatly that he would not be coming back. They have done a total 180 without any explanation, or any indication that concerns about legal and other liabilities have been resolved," Levine said in a telephone interview. 

"They have proven they're not independent, and that is the defining quality that we need from any board," he said.

Jan van Eck, a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) investor via the investment company bearing his name, said Huang's return likely removes uncertainty but amounts to a bet against further bad headlines.

"I had expected more of a Washington DC process, including Congressional hearings, to lengthen this determination, but I guess the Administration is willing to risk that there are no more bad facts to emerge," van Eck said in an email.   

QUESTIONS OF CANDOR

In addition to saying Huang's return posed no national security risk, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said that after discussions, it was "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA ( NVDA )."  

The company said an independent board committee is still investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and said "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion," with Huang's cooperation. The board has also taken steps like creating a new chief compliance officer position.

Nada Kakabadse, a Henley Business School professor who follows corporate governance, said the statement left gaps. " 'Satisfied with his candor' is a strange phrase while the investigation into what he told the company is still open. The board has reached its verdict before the evidence is in," Kakabadse said. 

Moreover, the board has given away much of the company's room for maneuver, she said. "It hands the board's judgment to the state. The same government that grants Nvidia's ( NVDA ) export licences now effectively vouches for its CEO. That makes the company politically dependent, and a future administration could withdraw the endorsement," she said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) board member Harvey Jones took the title of chair only this month. Until then, Nvidia ( NVDA ) was one of only two companies in the S&P 500 without a board chair, according to researcher Equilar. 

Corporate governance experts previously had said the setup and the presence of many long-serving directors meant the board would have to show it could act independently.  

Now, alongside relief at Huang's return, "there are sure to be questions about who is best placed to provide appropriate governance and oversight of key risks at the now-giant company at the center of a critically important global AI ecosystem," said Lindsey Stewart, Morningstar director of institutional insights. In reappointing Huang the board left those questions unanswered, Stewart said.

SKEPTICISM FROM SOME LAWMAKERS

US congressional committees will interview Huang on December 1. Lawmakers from both parties expressed skepticism about his return and the role of the administration. Some investors worried the political battles could overshadow Nvidia's ( NVDA ) commercial story.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America. Certain executives are going to be held to different standards," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer of Ocean Park Asset Management in California.  

Harvard Law School Professor Lucian Bebchuk said there was no indication the board had secured the support of Nvidia's largest shareholders, nominally the owners of the company. (Top fund firms BlackRock and Vanguard did not comment for this story.) 

Bebchuk said recent policies put in place by Trump-appointed regulators make it harder for big fund firms to weigh in on corporate governance issues.

Even if Huang poses no national security risks in the future, his actions to date could still entangle him and the company in costly investigations, Bebchuk said.

"The board presumably feels now vindicated by the immediate stock price increase following this morning's announcement. However, the board's reversal of its earlier decision raises serious questions and concerns," Bebchuk said.     

(Reporting by Ross Kerber in Boston and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Toby Sterling in Amsterdam and Chibuike Oguh in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Court To Overturn Marijuana Rescheduling Order? MMJ Citing Immediate And Irreparable Economic Harm
data.description:
WASHINGTON, D.C. / ACCESS Newswire / November 25, 2026 / MMJ International Holdings, Inc. ("MMJIH"), together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc. (collectively, "MMJ"), and a coalition of injured parties, filed their opening brief yesterday in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit seeking to hold unlawful and set aside Attorney General Order No. 6754-2026 rescheduling marijuana.

The litigation challenges the legality of the April 28, 2026 Order, which established a separate federal regulatory pathway for state-licensed medical marijuana businesses while companies pursuing the established federal pharmaceutical development pathway remain subject to extensive FDA and DEA requirements.

MMJ occupies a distinct position among the petitioners: it is a commercial pharmaceutical developer alleging direct and continuing economic injury resulting from the Order.

THE ECONOMIC DAMAGE IS HAPPENING NOW

"MMJ is not hurt by what this Order might do someday. We are hurt by what it is doing right now," stated Duane Boise, President and Chief Executive Officer of MMJ International Holdings.

"For eight years and more than $10 million, MMJ has pursued the federal regulatory pathway to develop pharmaceutical medicines from marijuana. We filed our FDA Investigational New Drug applications, secured an Orphan Drug Designation, established a DEA-registered Schedule I analytical laboratory and manufactured a finished pharmaceutical soft-gel capsule.

"That investment in federal compliance was supposed to be our competitive advantage. Instead, the government has turned it into a competitive disadvantage."

State marijuana operators are already receiving DEA registrations, while certain publicly traded operators have announced that they are no longer applying the federal tax restrictions imposed by Section 280E.

Meanwhile, thousands of state operators have applied for federal registrations under a framework that permits qualifying timely applicants to continue operating while their applications remain pending.

"Our competitors are already realizing regulatory and economic benefits while MMJ continues to wait for its federal bulk-manufacturer registration," Boise continued.

"Investors are already questioning why the federal government has extended these benefits to businesses that bypassed federal requirements. Every day this Order remains in effect, MMJ's competitive position, investment value and pharmaceutical market opportunity are being eroded. A later court ruling cannot necessarily restore what has already been lost."

THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT IS PENALIZING COMPLIANCE

MMJ has invested more than eight years and $10 million in scientific research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, analytical testing, regulatory submissions and clinical development.

Its regulatory and pharmaceutical milestones include:

  • Two FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) applications targeting Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis.
  • FDA Orphan Drug Designation for its Huntington's disease drug development program.
  • A DEA Schedule I analytical laboratory registration and Rhode Island laboratory license CAL00016.
  • Manufacturing of 50,000 pharmaceutical-grade THC/CBD soft-gel capsules under Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
  • Rhode Island cultivation/manufacturing licensure .
  • A pending DEA bulk-manufacturer application originally submitted in December 2018.

While MMJ has invested in standardized formulations, pharmaceutical manufacturing, stability testing and regulatory compliance, state dispensaries are already selling cannabinoid capsules, tablets and other products marketed for therapeutic purposes without those products necessarily undergoing equivalent FDA drug-development review.

MMJ contends that the Order creates an unequal competitive environment that undermines the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, effective and scientifically validated cannabinoid medicines.

FIVE FUNDAMENTAL LEGAL CHALLENGES TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S ORDER

The petitioners' opening brief challenges the Order on multiple statutory and administrative-law grounds, arguing that it:

  1. Violates the Controlled Substances Act by assigning marijuana to different schedules based on state licensing status rather than the statutory scheduling criteria.
  2. Bypasses required federal rulemaking procedures under 21 U.S.C. § 811, raising issues addressed by the D.C. Circuit in NORML v. DEA (1977), as well as questions concerning the scope of the Attorney General's statutory authority.
  3. Conflicts with international drug treaty obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961, including requirements governing cultivation, production quotas, government oversight, crop possession, distribution and medical prescriptions.
  4. Rewrites federal controlled-substance regulations without required notice-and-comment rulemaking, establishing alternative regulatory requirements for state marijuana businesses.
  5. Reverses previous federal regulatory positions without adequate explanation, including concerns previously identified by DEA regarding diversion, public safety and inconsistent regulatory standards across state marijuana programs.

These challenges raise fundamental questions about whether the Attorney General possessed the statutory authority to establish an alternative federal regulatory system for an existing state marijuana industry.

DEA'S OWN FINDINGS RAISE QUESTIONS ABOUT STATE REGULATORY SAFEGUARDS

The Attorney General's Order asserts that state medical marijuana regulatory systems have developed robust infrastructure for preventing diversion, ensuring product safety, maintaining records and conducting facility inspections.

Yet DEA's own 2025 National Drug Threat Assessment documents marijuana trafficking from states where marijuana is legal under state law into other jurisdictions and identifies vulnerabilities exploited by criminal organizations.

Additionally, recent litigation brought by state marijuana operators themselves has highlighted the difficulties of reconciling existing state marijuana supply chains with federal controlled-substance requirements and international treaty obligations.

MMJ believes these developments raise serious questions about the factual and legal foundations of the Attorney General's Order.

"The issue has never been whether marijuana has therapeutic potential," Boise stated. "The issue is whether the federal government can abandon established regulatory safeguards, reward businesses that historically operated outside federal law and economically injure companies that followed the law."

INTERNATIONAL DRUG TREATY OBLIGATIONS ARE NOT OPTIONAL

MMJ maintains that the United States cannot disregard its obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs simply to accommodate an established commercial marijuana industry.

Federal oversight of marijuana cultivation, production quotas, inventory, distribution and medical use raises significant legal questions that cannot be resolved merely by recognizing existing state licenses.

MMJ's pharmaceutical development program has been structured around established federal controls governing controlled substances intended for medical and scientific purposes.

"MMJ built its business around federal law. The state marijuana industry built its business around state law despite federal prohibition. Now the federal government is attempting to reconcile those two fundamentally different systems at the expense of companies that complied with federal requirements," Boise said.

MMJ SEEKS SWIFT JUDICIAL RELIEF

MMJ joins the States of Nebraska and Indiana, Smart Approaches to Marijuana (SAM), the National Drug and Alcohol Screening Association (NDASA), New Directions Addiction Recovery Services, Cannabis Industry Victims Educating Litigators (CIVEL), and Drs. Kenneth Finn and Elizabeth Stuyt in challenging the Attorney General's Order.

MMJ is represented by Burke Law Group, PLLC.

The company hopes the D.C. Circuit will swiftly remedy its injury, as MMJ continues to suffer economic and competitive harm for as long as the Order remains in effect.

"This is not a fight against marijuana rescheduling. It is a fight against unlawful rescheduling, unequal regulatory treatment and the destruction of the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, scientifically validated pharmaceutical medicines," Boise concluded.

"Federal compliance should be rewarded - not punished."

About MMJ International Holdings

MMJ International Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc., based in Westerly, Rhode Island, is a pharmaceutical development company focused on standardized cannabinoid medicines derived from natural marijuana extracts through established FDA and DEA regulatory pathways.

Its clinical development programs target serious neurological conditions, including Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis, using GMP-manufactured THC/CBD soft-gel capsules designed for clinical trials.
